# Generate 10 Bakery Opening Social Media Posts with Cohere

> **In short:** Type a clear prompt into Cohere's chat playground with your bakery's name, vibe and opening date, and you'll get back 10 editable social media post ideas for your opening week. Free tier is enough; you write the final copy and pick the visuals yourself.

If you're opening a small bakery and the social media calendar feels empty, this walkthrough shows you how to ask Cohere (a large language model — an AI that writes text the way ChatGPT does) for a full week of post ideas in one go. You'll give it the basics — name, vibe, opening date — and edit the results to match your real voice.

## Before you start
- A free Cohere account (sign up with email or Google at cohere.com — no credit card needed for the trial tier).
- A browser on a phone or computer with internet access.
- A few details already decided: your bakery's name, the feeling you want it to give off (cozy, modern, playful, etc.) and your opening date.
- Roughly 15–20 minutes for your first run.

## Step 1 — Open the Cohere chat playground
Go to **cohere.com** in your browser and click the **Sign in** or **Get started** button at the top-right corner. After you log in, look for a link or button labeled **Playground**, **Chat** or **Try it** — Cohere sometimes places this in the top navigation, sometimes on your dashboard. Click it. A chat window opens with a blank text box at the bottom, ready for you to type a message. If you're new, the page may show a short tour; you can skip it.
💬 Example: there is nothing to type yet — just open the page.
You'll know it worked when you see a message input box at the bottom of the screen with a blinking cursor and a send button (usually a small arrow or paper-plane icon).

## Step 2 — Gather your three key details
Before you write the prompt, grab a piece of paper or open a notes app and write down three things: (1) your bakery's name, (2) one or two words that describe the vibe you want (warm and rustic, sleek and modern, fun and kid-friendly), and (3) your exact opening date. These three details are the seed information — the basic facts you feed in — that the AI will use to shape every post idea. If you skip this step, you'll spend more time retyping in the chat. Think of it like writing a shopping list before you go to the store.
💬 Example: name "Honey & Crumb", vibe "cozy neighborhood bakery, slow mornings", date "Saturday, 12 April 2026".
You'll know it worked when you can read the three details out loud in one sentence without stopping to think.

## Step 3 — Paste your first prompt into the chat
Click inside the chat text box at the bottom of the page. Type or paste a short instruction that tells Cohere exactly what you want. Keep it simple, specific and friendly. Mention the role you want the AI to play, your three details, and the number of ideas you want. Hit the **send** button (the arrow or paper-plane icon). Cohere will start typing a response within a few seconds. If you can't find the send button, try pressing the **Enter** key on your keyboard.
💬 Example: "You are a social media manager for a small bakery called Honey & Crumb. The vibe is cozy, neighborhood, slow mornings. We open Saturday, 12 April 2026. Give me 10 social media post ideas for the opening week. For each post include: the platform, a 1–2 sentence caption, and a short visual idea."
You'll know it worked when Cohere returns a numbered list of 10 distinct post ideas, each with a platform, a caption and a visual suggestion.

## Step 4 — Read through and flag your favorites
Read every idea, even the ones that feel off. As you read, copy the ones you like into your notes app, or mentally star them. Look for variety: an opening-day announcement, a behind-the-scenes peek, a "meet the baker" post, a giveaway, a menu teaser, and so on. If several posts feel too generic (like "come visit us!"), that's normal — you'll fix them in the next step. If the whole response is in a tone you don't like (too formal, too salesy), note one or two words that describe the tone you DO want.
💬 Example: highlight posts #1, #3, #4 and #7 in your notes; mark posts #2 and #9 as "too generic — needs personality".
You'll know it worked when you have at least 4–5 posts worth editing and a clear sense of which ideas need a rewrite.

## Step 5 — Ask Cohere to rewrite the weak ones
In the same chat (don't start a new one — the AI remembers your bakery details), type a follow-up message asking it to redo the weak posts in your preferred tone. Be specific about what to change. Press **Enter** or tap send. Cohere will replace those ideas with new versions that build on everything you've already discussed. If the second version still isn't right, try a third time with even more guidance, such as "make it sound like a friend talking, not an ad." This back-and-forth is the normal way to work with an AI — your first try is rarely the last.
💬 Example: "Rewrite posts #2 and #9 in a friendlier, less salesy tone — like a regular customer telling their neighbor about a new spot. Keep the same visual ideas."
You'll know it worked when the rewritten posts feel closer to how you actually talk about your bakery.

## Step 6 — Copy your final list and schedule it
Highlight the full final response, copy it with **Ctrl+C** (Windows) or **Cmd+C** (Mac), and paste it into a Google Doc, a spreadsheet or your social media scheduling tool of choice. Add a column for the date each post will go live across the opening week — Monday teaser, Wednesday menu reveal, Friday opening day, and so on. Add images later; for now you have the words. Cohere cannot post to Instagram or Facebook for you, and it cannot generate the photos — you'll handle those parts yourself, but the hard thinking part is done.
💬 Example: paste into a sheet with columns for Date | Platform | Caption | Visual idea, then fill in a date for each row.
You'll know it worked when you have a clean one-page calendar with 10 captions ready to schedule, edit or photograph around.

## Common mistakes
- **Vague prompt, vague result.** Asking "give me bakery social media posts" returns generic fluff. Always include the name, vibe, date and a number — those four details turn the AI from a stranger into a focused assistant.
- **Throwing away the first response.** The first list is a draft, not the final version. Treat it like a brainstorm with a coworker who types fast — pick the good, send back the rest for a rewrite.
- **Posting the AI text word-for-word.** Cohere's writing is a starting point, not your voice. Read every caption out loud; if it doesn't sound like you, change it. Readers can tell when a small business sounds like a press release.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** You can use the same prompt pattern any time you face a blank page — birthday invitations, neighborhood announcements, school event flyers — by swapping in your details and the number of ideas you need.
- **For your business or work:** A weekly content block takes 20 minutes instead of 2 hours. You still pick the photos and have the final say, but the thinking and drafting is no longer the slow part.
- **If you're just getting started:** Save the prompt from Step 3 as a template. Next week, paste it in again with this week's details, and you'll get fresh ideas in seconds.

## Try it now
Open Cohere's playground, copy the example prompt from Step 3, replace the three details with your own bakery's information, and hit send. Your 10 opening-week post ideas will be on the screen in under a minute.
